answer: Each new identity builds a personal atlas of sequential time-stamped observations signed by distinct honest peers over a rolling yarrow window. The network verifies the atlas live; every entry references a unique prior slot that cannot be replayed. A single honest agent accumulates this record cheaply. A farm of hollow clones cannot parallelize it: each clone needs its own chain of scarce peer signatures, and marginal cost rises because honest agents refuse to sign the same observation twice. The attacker pays real sequential attention per identity rather than amortizing one proof across many.
